modules.title: Complex Structures
modules.description: Master intermediate grammar patterns including passive voice, causative form, conditionals, and expressions of change and effort.

lessons.title: Passive Voice (受身)
lessons.description: Learn to form and use the passive voice with ～られる and ～あれる constructions.

content.title: How to Form the Passive Voice

body.html:
The passive voice in Japanese is formed by changing the verb ending:

  • Group 1 (五段): Change the final -u to -areru. 書く → 書かれる, 読む → 読まれる, 飲む → 飲まれる
  • Group 2 (一段): Drop -ru and add -rareru. 食べる → 食べられる, 見る → 見られる
  • Irregular: する → される, 来る → 来られる

The passive is used for: (1) actions received from others, (2) suffering or inconvenience (迷惑の受身), and (3) neutral/formal descriptions of events.

Structure: （受け手）は（動作主）に（動詞の受身形）

Example: 私は先生に褒められた。(I was praised by the teacher.)
tips: The particle に marks the agent (doer) in passive sentences.
The 'suffering passive' (迷惑の受身) expresses that the action negatively affected the subject: 雨に降られた (I got rained on).
Group 2 passive ～られる is identical to the potential form — context tells them apart.

body.question: Choose the correct passive form of 「母が私を起こした」 (My mother woke me up) rewritten from my perspective.
body.explanation: In passive voice, the agent (母) takes the particle に, and the verb 起こす becomes 起こされる. The subject (私) takes は.

body.translation: My cake was eaten by my younger brother. (suffering passive)

lessons.title: Causative Form (使役)
lessons.description: Learn to express making or letting someone do something using ～させる and ～あせる.

body.html:
The causative form expresses 'make someone do' or 'let someone do' something:

  • Group 1 (五段): Change the final -u to -aseru. 書く → 書かせる, 読む → 読ませる, 行く → 行かせる
  • Group 2 (一段): Drop -ru and add -saseru. 食べる → 食べさせる, 見る → 見させる
  • Irregular: する → させる, 来る → 来させる

Key particle patterns:

  • Transitive verbs: AはBにCを（causative）— 先生は学生にレポートを書かせた。
  • Intransitive verbs: AはBを（causative）— 母は子供を外で遊ばせた。

Whether it means 'make' or 'let' depends on context. Adding ～てあげる or ～てください often signals 'let'.
tips: ～させてください means 'please let me do ~': やらせてください (Please let me do it).
With intransitive verbs, the 'causee' is marked with を, not に.
The causative-passive (～させられる) means 'was made to do' — very common in N3.

body.sentence: 先生は学生に本を＿＿＿。(The teacher made the students read the book.)
body.explanation: 読む (yomu, Group 1) → 読ませる (yomaseru). Past tense: 読ませた. The teacher (先生) causes the students (学生) to read (読む) the book (本).

body.question: What does 「子供を寝させた」 mean?
body.explanation: 寝る → 寝させる (causative). 子供を寝させた = (I) made the child sleep. The particle を marks the causee with intransitive verbs.

lessons.title: Conditional: ば and たら
lessons.description: Master two essential conditional patterns for expressing 'if' in Japanese.

content.title: ば vs たら — Two Ways to Say 'If'

body.html:
Japanese has multiple conditional forms. The two most important at N3 are ～ば and ～たら.

～ば (Hypothetical condition)

  • Verbs: Change final -u to -eba. 行く → 行けば, 食べる → 食べれば
  • i-adjectives: Drop final い, add ければ. 高い → 高ければ
  • na-adj/nouns: + であれば / ならば

Used for general/logical conditions: 勉強すれば、受かる。(If you study, you'll pass.)

～たら (Realized condition)

  • Take the past form (た) and add ら. 行った → 行ったら, 食べた → 食べたら

Used when the 'if' is more concrete or temporal: 家に帰ったら、電話してください。(When/if you get home, please call me.)

Key Difference

～ば is more hypothetical and general; ～たら is more concrete and often implies temporal sequence ('when' or 'after').
tips: ～ば cannot be used when the main clause is a request, invitation, or volitional action (use ～たら instead).
～たら is the safest, most versatile conditional — when in doubt, use ～たら.
ば is preferred for proverbs and universal truths: 塵も積もれば山となる。

body.question: Fill in the blank: 「もっと早く＿＿、間に合ったのに。」 (If I had left earlier, I would have made it in time.)
body.explanation: This sentence describes a specific past situation that didn't happen (counterfactual). ～たら is used for concrete, realized (or hypothetically realized) conditions. 出たら = 'if (I) had left'.

body.sentence: 天気が＿＿＿、ピクニックに行きましょう。(If the weather is good, let's go on a picnic.)
body.explanation: 良い (いい/よい) → よければ. For the ば conditional of い-adjectives, drop い and add ければ.

lessons.title: ようにする / ようになる
lessons.description: Express making an effort to do something and describing natural changes in ability or habit.

body.html:
These two patterns look similar but express very different ideas:

～ようにする (Make an effort to ~)

Expresses a conscious effort or decision to do/not do something regularly.

  • 毎日運動するようにしている。(I make an effort to exercise every day.)
  • 甘いものを食べないようにしている。(I try not to eat sweets.)

～ようになる (Come to ~ / Become able to ~)

Expresses a natural, gradual change in state, ability, or habit.

  • 日本語が話せるようになった。(I became able to speak Japanese.)
  • 最近、早く起きるようになった。(Lately I've started waking up early.)

Key: ようにする = deliberate action; ようになる = natural/gradual change.
tips: ようにしている (progressive) emphasizes an ongoing habit/effort.
ようになる often pairs with potential forms: 読めるようになった (became able to read).
Negative form: ～ないようにする (try not to ~) / ～なくなる (stop doing ~, naturally).

content.title: ようにする vs ようになる

body.question: Which sentence means 'I became able to understand Japanese news'?
options: 日本語のニュースがわかるようにしている。
日本語のニュースがわかるようになった。
日本語のニュースがわかるようにした。
日本語のニュースがわかるようにする。
body.explanation: ～ようになった expresses a gradual, natural change — 'came to be able to ~'. The other options involve deliberate effort (ようにする).

content.title: Build a ようにする Sentence

body.translation: I make an effort not to be late.

flashcardDecks.title: N3 Grammar Patterns
flashcardDecks.description: 25 essential N3-level grammar patterns covering passive, causative, conditionals, and complex expressions.

back.text: Passive voice — indicates receiving an action
back.example: 私は先生に褒められた。(I was praised by the teacher.)
back.notes: Group 1: -u → -areru; Group 2: -ru → -rareru; する → される

back.example: 母は子供に野菜を食べさせた。(The mother made the child eat vegetables.)
back.notes: Group 1: -u → -aseru; Group 2: -ru → -saseru; する → させる

back.text: Causative-passive — be made to do something (often unwillingly)
back.example: 無理やり歌わせられた。(I was forced to sing.)
back.notes: Causative + passive combined. Very common in conversation.

back.example: 安ければ買います。(If it's cheap, I'll buy it.)
back.notes: Verbs: -u → -eba; い-adj: drop い + ければ

back.example: 駅に着いたら電話してください。(When you arrive at the station, please call.)
back.notes: Past form (た) + ら. Most versatile conditional.

back.text: Make an effort to ~; try to ~ (deliberate)
back.example: 毎日野菜を食べるようにしている。(I make an effort to eat vegetables every day.)
back.notes: Dict-form/ない-form + ようにする

back.text: Come to ~; become able to ~ (natural change)
back.example: 漢字が読めるようになった。(I became able to read kanji.)
back.notes: Dict-form/potential + ようになる. Gradual change.

back.example: 来月から日本語を勉強することにした。(I decided to study Japanese from next month.)
back.notes: Dict-form/ない-form + ことにする

back.text: It has been decided that ~ (external/group decision)
back.example: 来年、東京に転勤することになった。(It's been decided I'll transfer to Tokyo next year.)
back.notes: The decision is presented as beyond one's control.

back.text: End up doing ~; do ~ completely (often with regret)
back.example: 財布を忘れてしまった。(I ended up forgetting my wallet.)
back.notes: Casual: ～ちゃう/～じゃう. Can express completion or regret.

back.text: Should be ~; is expected to ~ (based on reason/evidence)
back.example: 彼はもう来ているはずだ。(He should be here already.)
back.notes: Dict-form/ない/noun の/na-adj な + はずだ

back.example: 毎日練習したわけだから、上手になったわけだ。(Since you practiced every day, no wonder you got good.)
back.notes: わけがない = there's no way ~; わけにはいかない = can't possibly ~

back.text: Just as ~; in the way that ~
back.example: 言われたとおりにやりました。(I did it just as I was told.)
back.notes: Noun の / Dict-form/た-form + とおりに

back.example: 試験に受かるために勉強する。(I study in order to pass the exam.)
back.notes: Dict-form + ために (purpose); た-form/noun の + ために (cause)

back.text: So that ~; in order to ~ (with non-volitional verbs)
back.example: 聞こえるように大きい声で話した。(I spoke loudly so that it could be heard.)
back.notes: Used when the goal verb is non-volitional. Cf. ～ために for volitional.

back.text: Something has been done (resultant state, with purpose)
back.example: 窓が開けてある。(The window has been opened [on purpose].)
back.notes: Transitive verb て-form + ある. Object takes が.

back.text: Do ~ in advance; leave ~ as is (preparation)
back.example: ホテルを予約しておいた。(I reserved a hotel in advance.)
back.notes: Casual: ～とく. Implies doing something for future benefit.

back.example: もっと勉強すればよかった。(I should have studied more.)
back.notes: ば conditional + よかった. Expresses regret about the past.

back.example: 雨が降っても行きます。(Even if it rains, I'll go.)
back.notes: て-form + も. い-adj: くても; な-adj/noun: でも

back.example: 約束したのに、来なかった。(Although (he) promised, (he) didn't come.)
back.notes: Plain form + のに. Carries an emotional nuance — frustration, surprise.

back.text: Change approaching the present (くる) / moving away from the present (いく)
back.example: だんだん寒くなってきた。(It has gradually gotten cold.)
back.notes: ～てくる = change up to now; ～ていく = change from now on.

back.text: Sometimes ~; there are times when ~ (occasional occurrence)
back.example: 朝ごはんを食べないことがある。(There are times I don't eat breakfast.)
back.notes: Dict-form + ことがある. Cf. た-form + ことがある = 'have experienced ~'.

back.example: 行くかどうかまだ決めていない。(I haven't decided whether or not to go.)
back.notes: Plain form + かどうか. Used for embedded yes/no questions.

back.example: もっと早く来てほしい。(I want (you) to come earlier.)
back.notes: （person に）て-form + ほしい. ないでほしい = I want (you) not to ~.

back.text: About to ~ / in the middle of ~ / just finished ~
back.example: 今から出かけるところだ。(I'm about to go out now.)
back.notes: Dict-form + ところ (about to); ている + ところ (in the middle); た + ところ (just did)

modules.title: Society & Culture
modules.description: Build vocabulary related to news, environment, feelings, and abstract concepts commonly tested at N3 level.

lessons.title: News & Media
lessons.description: Learn vocabulary used in news reports, media, and journalism.

body.html:
At the N3 level, you're expected to understand news headlines and simple articles. Key vocabulary includes:

  • ニュース — news
  • 新聞（しんぶん）— newspaper
  • 放送（ほうそう）— broadcast
  • 記事（きじ）— article
  • 報道（ほうどう）— news report
  • 番組（ばんぐみ）— (TV/radio) program
  • 情報（じょうほう）— information
  • 事件（じけん）— incident, case

Example: 今朝のニュースで大きな事件が報道された。
(A major incident was reported on this morning's news.)
tips: 報道 is more formal than ニュース — used in official reporting contexts.
番組 is specific to TV/radio programs, while 記事 is for written articles.
情報 is a very versatile word: 個人情報 (personal information), 情報社会 (information society).

body.question: テレビの＿＿＿で料理の作り方を見ました。(I watched how to cook on a TV _____.)
body.explanation: 番組（ばんぐみ）means TV/radio program. 記事 is a written article, 新聞 is a newspaper, and 報道 is a formal news report.

body.sentence: インターネットで最新の＿＿＿を調べた。(I looked up the latest ___ on the internet.)
body.explanation: 情報（じょうほう）means 'information'. It's commonly paired with 最新 (latest) in everyday usage.

lessons.title: Environment
lessons.description: Vocabulary for discussing nature, environmental issues, and their effects.

body.html:
Environmental topics appear frequently in N3 reading passages. Master these core words:

  • 自然（しぜん）— nature
  • 環境（かんきょう）— environment
  • 問題（もんだい）— problem, issue
  • 影響（えいきょう）— influence, effect
  • 温暖化（おんだんか）— global warming
  • 汚染（おせん）— pollution
  • 資源（しげん）— resources
  • エネルギー — energy

Example: 環境問題は私たちの生活に大きな影響を与えている。
(Environmental issues are having a major impact on our lives.)
tips: 影響を与える (to give influence = to have an effect) and 影響を受ける (to receive influence = to be affected) are key collocations.
環境問題 is a compound: 環境 (environment) + 問題 (problem).
自然 can be a noun ('nature') or a な-adjective ('natural'): 自然な笑顔 (a natural smile).

body.translation: We should think about environmental issues.

body.question: 「温暖化」の意味は何ですか。(What does 温暖化 mean?)
body.explanation: 温暖化（おんだんか）means 'warming' — specifically global warming (地球温暖化). 温暖 = warm, 化 = -ification/change.

lessons.title: Feelings & Character
lessons.description: Express emotions, personality traits, and psychological states.

body.html:
Describing emotions and personality requires a rich vocabulary at N3 level:

  • 気持ち（きもち）— feeling, mood
  • 性格（せいかく）— personality, character
  • 心配（しんぱい）— worry, concern
  • 安心（あんしん）— relief, peace of mind
  • 感動（かんどう）— being deeply moved/impressed
  • 我慢（がまん）— patience, endurance
  • 自信（じしん）— self-confidence
  • 緊張（きんちょう）— nervousness, tension

Many of these function as both nouns and する-verbs:

試験の前に緊張した。 (I got nervous before the exam.)
結果を聞いて安心した。 (I felt relieved after hearing the result.)
tips: 心配する = to worry (about); 心配をかける = to cause someone worry.
我慢する is 'to endure/put up with' — 我慢できない = I can't stand it.
感動する = to be moved/touched; 感動的 = moving/touching (adjective).

body.sentence: 彼女は明るい＿＿＿で、みんなに好かれている。(She has a bright _____ and is liked by everyone.)
body.explanation: 性格（せいかく）means personality/character. 明るい性格 = bright/cheerful personality.

body.question: 「感動した」とはどういう意味ですか。(What does 感動した mean?)
body.explanation: 感動する（かんどうする）means to be deeply moved or impressed. 感 = feeling, 動 = move.

lessons.title: Abstract Concepts
lessons.description: Learn words for discussing opportunities, goals, experiences, and outcomes.

body.html:
At N3, you need words to discuss abstract ideas in essays, conversations, and reading passages:

  • 機会（きかい）— opportunity, chance
  • 目的（もくてき）— purpose, objective
  • 経験（けいけん）— experience
  • 結果（けっか）— result, outcome
  • 原因（げんいん）— cause, reason
  • 関係（かんけい）— relationship, connection
  • 状況（じょうきょう）— situation, circumstances
  • 条件（じょうけん）— condition, requirement

Example: 失敗の原因を調べて、結果を報告してください。
(Please investigate the cause of the failure and report the results.)
tips: 機会 vs チャンス: 機会 is more formal. 機会があれば (if I have the chance).
原因 (cause) and 結果 (result) often appear together: 原因と結果の関係 (cause-and-effect relationship).
経験する = to experience (する-verb). いい経験になった = It was a good experience.

body.question: 日本に留学した＿＿＿は、とても良かったです。(The _____ of studying abroad in Japan was very good.)
body.explanation: 経験（けいけん）means 'experience'. The sentence describes the experience of studying abroad. 結果 = result, 目的 = purpose, 条件 = condition.

body.translation: We are investigating the cause of the accident.

flashcardDecks.title: N3 Vocabulary: Society & Culture
flashcardDecks.description: 25 essential N3-level vocabulary words covering news, environment, feelings, and abstract concepts.

back.example: 毎朝ニュースを見ている。(I watch the news every morning.)
back.notes: Noun (katakana loanword from English)

back.example: 父は毎朝新聞を読む。(My father reads the newspaper every morning.)
back.notes: Noun

back.example: その番組は生放送だった。(That program was a live broadcast.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb. 生放送 = live broadcast

back.example: この記事は面白い。(This article is interesting.)
back.notes: Noun

back.example: テレビで事故の報道を見た。(I saw a news report about the accident on TV.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb. More formal than ニュース.

back.example: 好きな番組は何ですか。(What's your favorite program?)
back.notes: Noun

back.example: 正確な情報が必要だ。(Accurate information is needed.)
back.notes: Noun. 個人情報 = personal information

back.example: この町は自然が豊かだ。(This town is rich in nature.)
back.notes: Noun / な-adjective. 自然な = natural (adj)

back.example: 環境を守ることが大切だ。(It's important to protect the environment.)
back.notes: Noun. 環境問題 = environmental issue

back.example: 睡眠不足は健康に影響を与える。(Lack of sleep has an effect on health.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb. 影響を与える = to affect; 影響を受ける = to be affected

back.example: 地球温暖化が心配されている。(Global warming is a concern.)
back.notes: Noun. 温暖 = warm + 化 = -ification

back.example: 大気汚染が深刻だ。(Air pollution is serious.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb. 大気汚染 = air pollution; 水質汚染 = water pollution

back.example: 資源を大切に使おう。(Let's use resources carefully.)
back.notes: Noun. 天然資源 = natural resources

back.example: あなたの気持ちはわかります。(I understand your feelings.)
back.notes: Noun. 気持ちがいい = feels good; 気持ちが悪い = feels bad/unpleasant

back.example: 彼はやさしい性格だ。(He has a gentle personality.)
back.notes: Noun

back.example: 心配しないでください。(Please don't worry.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb / な-adjective. 心配をかける = to cause worry

back.example: 無事と聞いて安心した。(I was relieved to hear (you're) safe.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb. Opposite of 心配.

back.example: 映画に感動して泣いた。(I was moved by the movie and cried.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb. 感動的な = moving, touching

back.example: 痛いけど我慢した。(It hurt but I endured it.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb. 我慢できない = I can't stand it

back.example: 機会があれば、ぜひ参加したい。(If there's an opportunity, I'd definitely like to participate.)
back.notes: Noun. More formal than チャンス.

back.example: 旅行の目的は何ですか。(What is the purpose of the trip?)
back.notes: Noun. 目的地 = destination

back.example: いい経験になった。(It was a good experience.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb. 経験者 = experienced person

back.example: 試験の結果を待っている。(I'm waiting for the exam results.)
back.notes: Noun. その結果 = as a result

back.example: 事故の原因はまだわからない。(The cause of the accident is still unknown.)
back.notes: Noun. Often paired with 結果: 原因と結果

back.example: 二人の関係はとてもいい。(Their relationship is very good.)
back.notes: Noun / する-verb. 関係がある = to be related; 関係ない = unrelated

modules.title: Nuanced Communication
modules.description: Master sentence patterns for formal requests, expressing uncertainty, and connecting ideas smoothly in conversation.

lessons.title: Formal Requests
lessons.description: Learn polite and formal ways to make requests in Japanese.

body.html:
N3-level requests go beyond basic ～てください. Here are patterns ranked from polite to very polite:

～くださいませんか (Would you please ~?)

More polite than ～てください. Uses negative question form for softness.

少々お待ちくださいませんか。 (Would you please wait a moment?)

～いただけませんか (Could I have you ~?)

Very polite. Uses the humble form いただく + potential + negative question.

この書類を確認していただけませんか。 (Could you check this document?)

お願いします (Please / I ask of you)

Versatile polite request. Can stand alone or follow a noun.

コーヒーをお願いします。 (Coffee, please.)

～ていただきたいのですが (I would like you to ~)

Indirect and very polite. The のですが softens the request further.

少し手伝っていただきたいのですが。 (I'd like you to help me a little, if you could...)
tips: Negative questions (～ませんか) are softer than positive ones — they give the listener room to decline.
いただく is the humble form of もらう; using it elevates the listener.
～のですが leaves the sentence trailing, making it even more indirect and polite.

body.question: Which is the MOST polite way to ask someone to explain?
options: 説明してくださいませんか。
説明していただけませんか。
body.explanation: ～していただけませんか uses the humble いただく in potential negative-question form, making it the most polite. して is casual, してください is standard polite, and してくださいませんか is polite.

body.sentence: すみません、写真を撮って＿＿＿＿＿＿。(Excuse me, could you take a photo?)
body.explanation: Both いただけませんか and くださいませんか are polite request forms. いただけませんか is slightly more polite as it uses the humble verb いただく.

lessons.title: Expressing Uncertainty
lessons.description: Use らしい, よう, みたい, and っぽい to express conjecture and hearsay.

body.html:
Japanese has several expressions for uncertainty, each with a different nuance:

～らしい (Hearsay / seems like, based on information)

Based on information heard or read. Not firsthand observation.

田中さんは来週結婚するらしい。 (Apparently Tanaka-san is getting married next week.)

～ようだ (Appears to be ~, based on observation)

Based on the speaker's own observation or judgment. More formal.

彼は疲れているようだ。 (He appears to be tired.)

～みたいだ (Seems like ~, casual version of ようだ)

Same meaning as ようだ but more casual and conversational.

外は寒いみたいだ。 (It seems cold outside.)

～っぽい (Looks like ~; -ish; tends to be ~)

Casual suffix. Can also express tendency or characteristic.

この色は子供っぽい。 (This color is childish.)
tips: らしい attaches to plain form (verbs, adjectives, nouns — no だ for nouns/na-adj).
ようだ is preceded by noun の / na-adj な, but みたいだ follows nouns directly.
っぽい conjugates like an い-adjective: 子供っぽくない (not childish).
～らしい after a noun can also mean 'typical of': 男らしい (manly), 学生らしい (student-like).

body.question: 友達から聞いたんだけど、あの店は来月閉まる＿＿＿。(I heard from a friend that that shop is apparently closing next month.)
body.explanation: らしい is used for information obtained from others (hearsay). The key clue is 友達から聞いた (heard from a friend) — the information is secondhand.

body.question: Which sentence correctly uses っぽい?
options: 彼女は大人っぽい服を着ている。
このスープは辛いっぽい。
body.explanation: 大人っぽい = adult-like, mature (in appearance). っぽい is most naturally used to express a quality or tendency (忘れっぽい, 怒りっぽい, 子供っぽい). It conjugates as an い-adjective, so っぽいだ is incorrect.

lessons.title: Connecting Ideas
lessons.description: Use conjunctions and transitional phrases to build coherent, flowing sentences.

body.html:
Smooth, connected speech and writing requires mastering transitional expressions. Here are key N3-level conjunctions:

Contrast

  • しかし — However (formal)
  • でも — But (casual)
  • ところが — However / And yet (unexpected result)

Cause & Result

  • そのため — For that reason (formal)
  • それで — So; and then; therefore
  • したがって — Therefore; consequently (very formal)

Rephrasing & Addition

  • つまり — In other words; that is to say
  • しかも — Moreover; what's more
  • ついでに — While (you're) at it; incidentally

Example: 雨が降った。しかし、試合は中止にならなかった。
(It rained. However, the game was not cancelled.)
tips: しかし is written/formal; でも is spoken/casual. Don't use でも in essays.
ところが emphasizes that the result was unexpected: 練習した。ところが、負けた。(I practiced. And yet, I lost.)
ついでに is practical: 買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った。(While shopping, I stopped by the post office.)

body.sentence: 彼は日本語が上手だ。＿＿＿、中国語も話せる。(He's good at Japanese. Moreover, he can also speak Chinese.)
body.explanation: しかも means 'moreover' or 'what's more' — used to add surprising or impressive additional information.

body.question: 説明が長すぎた。＿＿＿、誰も理解できなかった。(The explanation was too long. _____, no one could understand.)
body.explanation: それで means 'so; therefore' — connecting a cause (too long) with its result (no one understood). つまり = in other words; しかも = moreover; ついでに = while at it.

flashcardDecks.title: N3 Key Sentence Patterns
flashcardDecks.description: 20 key sentence patterns for formal requests, expressing uncertainty, and connecting ideas at the N3 level.

back.example: ちょっと教えていただけませんか。(Could you please teach me a bit?)
back.notes: Humble いただく + potential + negative question. Very polite.

back.example: もう少し待ってくださいませんか。(Would you please wait a little longer?)
back.notes: More polite than ～てください. Negative question softens the request.

back.example: お会計をお願いします。(The check, please.)
back.notes: Can follow nouns directly. Universal polite request form.

back.text: I would like you to ~ (indirect, very polite)
back.example: 確認していただきたいのですが。(I'd like you to check this, if you could...)
back.notes: The trailing のですが makes it very soft and indirect.

back.example: 明日は雨が降るらしい。(Apparently it will rain tomorrow.)
back.notes: Based on secondhand information. Plain form + らしい (no だ for nouns).

back.text: It appears that ~; it seems ~ (based on observation)
back.example: 道が濡れているようだ。(The road appears to be wet.)
back.notes: More formal than みたいだ. Based on speaker's own observation.

back.text: It seems like ~ (casual, same as ようだ)
back.example: 彼は忙しいみたいだ。(He seems busy.)
back.notes: Casual version of ようだ. Follows plain form / nouns directly.

back.example: 最近忘れっぽくなった。(I've become forgetful lately.)
back.notes: Conjugates like い-adjective. 子供っぽい = childish; 怒りっぽい = quick to anger.

back.example: 努力した。しかし、合格できなかった。(I worked hard. However, I couldn't pass.)
back.notes: Written/formal. Use でも in casual speech.

back.example: 晴れると思った。ところが、大雨になった。(I thought it would be sunny. And yet, it poured.)
back.notes: Emphasizes that the result was contrary to expectation.

back.example: 電車が止まった。それで、タクシーに乗った。(The train stopped. So I took a taxi.)
back.notes: Connects cause to result. Neutral register.

back.example: 人口が増えている。そのため、住宅が不足している。(The population is growing. For that reason, there's a housing shortage.)
back.notes: More formal than それで. Common in essays and reports.

back.text: In other words; that is to say
back.example: 彼は私の母の兄だ。つまり、おじだ。(He's my mother's older brother. In other words, my uncle.)
back.notes: Used to rephrase or summarize what was just said.

back.example: この店は安い。しかも、おいしい。(This shop is cheap. What's more, it's delicious.)
back.notes: Adds surprising or noteworthy additional information.

back.text: While (you're) at it; incidentally; on the way
back.example: 銀行に行くついでに、薬局にも寄った。(While going to the bank, I also stopped by the pharmacy.)
back.notes: Doing something extra along the way or while doing something else.

back.example: 明日は雪が降るかもしれない。(It might snow tomorrow.)
back.notes: Plain form + かもしれない. Casual: かも.

back.example: 彼は知っているに違いない。(He must know.)
back.notes: Plain form + にちがいない. Strong conviction, like 'must be'.

back.example: 予算が不足している。したがって、計画を変更する必要がある。(The budget is insufficient. Therefore, we need to change the plan.)
back.notes: Very formal. Used in academic writing and official documents.

back.text: On the other hand; while; meanwhile
back.example: 都市は便利だ。一方、自然が少ない。(Cities are convenient. On the other hand, there's little nature.)
back.notes: Used to present a contrasting viewpoint or simultaneous situation.

back.example: 彼は頭がいい。その上、スポーツも得意だ。(He's smart. On top of that, he's good at sports.)
back.notes: Similar to しかも but slightly more formal.
